title: Temurah 28
description: Chapter 6, Kol HaAsurin, opens with animals forbidden for the altar that render any mixture forbidden; the Gemara asks why the mishna repeats rulings from Zevaḥim and Avoda Zara, derives the exclusions from “from the cattle, from the herd, from the flock,” discusses the coatings of idols and derogatory names for idolatry, and turns to Reish Lakish’s seven-year set-aside and Gideon’s bullock.
topics: 🚫 Mishna: animals forbidden for the altar render a mixture forbidden in any amount
🔁 Why teach it again? Zevaḥim 70b and 71a, Rav Shimi bar Ashi’s non-sacred and consecrated, and Avoda Zara 74a
⚖️ “From the cattle”: the a fortiori from a blemished animal, plowing with an ox and a donkey, and one witness
👁️ Rav Ashi: a blemish is conspicuous, and this disqualification is not
🪙 “From the herd”: the coatings of a prostitute’s payment, the price of a dog and a worshipped animal
🏷️ “And you shall destroy their name”: Beit Galya is called Beit Karya
🐂 Copulation and goring compared, and “corruption” in the school of Rabbi Yishmael
🌙 Reish Lakish’s seven-year set-aside, and what was permitted to Gideon that night

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ כָּל הָאֲסוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ אוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהֵן — הָרוֹבֵעַ וְהַנִּרְבָּע, וְהַמּוּקְצֶה וְהַנֶּעֱבָד, וְהָאֶתְנַן וְהַמְּחִיר, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם וְהַטְּרֵפָה, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן.

a2.he: אֵיזֶהוּ מוּקְצֶה? הַמּוּקְצֶה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הוּא אָסוּר וּמַה שֶּׁעָלָיו מוּתָּר. וְאֵיזֶהוּ הַנֶּעֱבָד? כֹּל שֶׁעוֹבְדִין אוֹתוֹ, הוּא וּמַה שֶּׁעָלָיו אָסוּר. וְזֶה וָזֶה מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר מָר: אוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהֵן, דְּלָא בָּטְלִי בְּרוּבָּא. תְּנֵינָא: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בְּחַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת אוֹ בְּשׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, אֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד בְּרִבּוֹא — יָמוּתוּ.

a5.he: הָכִי קָתָנֵי: נִתְעָרְבוּ בָּהֶן מֵחַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת, אוֹ שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל — אֲפִילּוּ בְּרִבּוֹא יָמוּתוּ.

a6.he: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָתָם הוּא דְּאִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה, אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָאו אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה — אֵימָא: לִיבְטֵל בְּרוּבָּא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a7.he: וְרוֹבַע וְנִרְבָּע נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא: נִתְעָרְבוּ רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע — יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵי יָפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין!

a8.he: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר לִי: חֲדָא בְּחוּלִּין, וַחֲדָא בְּקָדָשִׁים.

a9.he: וּצְרִיכִי, דְּאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים — מִשּׁוּם דִּמְאִיסִי, אֲבָל גַּבֵּי חוּלִּין — אֵימָא לִיבְטְלוּ.

a10.he: וּבְחוּלִּין נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא: וְאֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין וְאוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהֵן — יֵין נֶסֶךְ, וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְצִיפֳּרֵי מְצוֹרָע, וְעוֹרוֹת לְבוּבִין.

a11.he: וְשֵׂיעַר נָזִיר, וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר, וּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב, וְשׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, וְחוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה, וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין וְאוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהֵן!

a12.he: צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָתָם — דְּאִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה דְּלָא בָּטְלִי, אֲבָל הָכָא — לִיבְטְלִי.

a13.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הָכָא, דִּלְגָבוֹהַּ דִּמְאִיס, אֲבָל לְהֶדְיוֹט — אֵימָא: אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה לִיבְטְלוּ בְּרוּבָּא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a14.he: וְרוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע, מְנָלַן דַּאֲסִירִי לְגָבוֹהַּ? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״ — לְהוֹצִיא רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע.

a15.he: וַהֲלֹא דִין הוּא, וּמָה בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶבְדָה בּוֹ עֲבֵירָה פָּסוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע שֶׁנֶּעֶבְדָה בָּהֶן עֲבֵירָה — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאֲסוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ?!

a16.he: חוֹרֵשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר יוֹכִיחַ, שֶׁנֶּעֶבְדָה בּוֹ עֲבֵירָה, וּמוּתָּר לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ.

a17.he: מָה לְחוֹרֵשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר, שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין מִיתָה, תֹּאמַר בְּרוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע, שֶׁחַיָּיבִין מִיתָה.

a18.he: טוֹל לָךְ מָה שֶׁהֵבֵאתָה, הֲרֵי שֶׁנֶּעֶבְדָה בָּהֶן עֲבֵירָה בִּשְׁנֵי עֵדִים.

a19.he: נֶעֶבְדָה בָּהֶן עֲבֵירָה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד, אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבְּעָלִים, מִנַּיִן?

a20.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אֲנִי דָּן, וּמָה בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁאֵין הַתְרָאַת שְׁנֵי עֵדִים פּוֹסַלְתּוֹ מֵאֲכִילָה — הוֹדָאַת עֵד אֶחָד פּוֹסַלְתּוֹ מֵהַקְרָבָה, בְּרוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע שֶׁהוֹדָאַת שְׁנֵי עֵדִים פּוֹסַלְתּוֹ מֵאֲכִילָה — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁהוֹדָאַת עֵד אֶחָד פּוֹסַלְתּוֹ מֵהַקְרָבָה!

a21.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״ לְהוֹצִיא רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע, וְהָא אָתְיָא מִדִּינָא (לָא אָתְיָא)!

b1.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּדִינָא פִּירְכָא — מָה לְבַעַל מוּם שֶׁכֵּן מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר.

b2.he: תֹּאמַר בְּרוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע, שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר, הוֹאִיל וְאֵין מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר יְהֵא כָּשֵׁר לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״, לְהוֹצִיא רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע.

b3.he: מִן הַבָּקָר — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַנֶּעֱבָד, וַהֲלֹא דִין הוּא: וּמָה אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר שֶׁצִּיפּוּיָין מוּתָּרִין — הֵן אֲסוּרִין, נֶעֱבָד שֶׁצִּיפּוּיוֹ אָסוּר — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁהוּא אָסוּר?

b4.he: אוֹ חִילּוּף, וּמָה אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר שֶׁהֵן אֲסוּרִין — צִיפּוּיֵיהֶן מוּתָּרִין, נֶעֱבָד שֶׁמּוּתָּר — יְהֵא צִיפּוּיוֹ מוּתָּר?

b5.he: אִם כֵּן בִּיטַּלְתָּ ״לֹא תַחְמוֹד כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב עֲלֵיהֶם וְלָקַחְתָּ לָךְ״!

b6.he: אֲנִי אֲקַיְּימֶנּוּ: ״לֹא תַּחֲמוֹד כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב״ — בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים, אֲבָל בְּדָבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים, הוֹאִיל (וְהֵן) [וְהוּא] מוּתָּר — יָכוֹל יְהֵא צִיפּוּי מוּתָּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִן הַבָּקָר״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַנֶּעֱבָד.

b7.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חֲנַנְיָא: טַעְמָא דְּמַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא, הָא לָא מַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא — צִיפּוּי מוּתָּר? וְהָכְתִיב ״וְאִבַּדְתֶּם אֶת שְׁמָם״ — כֹּל הֶעָשׂוּי לִשְׁמָם!

b8.he: הָהוּא לְכַנּוֹת לָהֶם שֵׁם הוּא דַּאֲתָא: לְ״בֵית גַּלְיָא״ קוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ ״בֵּית כַּרְיָא״, ״פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ״ — ״פְּנֵי כֶלֶב״, ״עֵין כֹּל״ — ״עֵין קוֹץ״.

b9.he: וְאֵיפוֹךְ אֲנָא: ״מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַנֶּעֱבָד, ״מִן הַבָּקָר״ — לְהוֹצִיא רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע!

b10.he: הָתָם מֵעִנְיָינָא דִּקְרָא, כְּתִיב גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִתֵּן שְׁכׇבְתּוֹ בִּבְהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת״, גַּבֵּי בָּקָר כְּתִיב ״וַיָּמִירוּ אֶת כְּבוֹדָם בְּתַבְנִית שׁוֹר אוֹכֵל עֵשֶׂב״.

b11.he: ״מִן הַצֹּאן״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַמּוּקְצֶה, ״וּמִן הַצֹּאן״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַנּוֹגֵחַ. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִם נֶאֱמַר רוֹבֵעַ — לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר נוֹגֵחַ? וְאִם נֶאֱמַר נוֹגֵחַ — לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר רוֹבֵעַ?

b12.he: לְפִי שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בָּרוֹבֵעַ, מָה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בַּנּוֹגֵחַ. יֵשׁ בָּרוֹבֵעַ, שֶׁהָרוֹבֵעַ עוֹשֶׂה אוֹנֶס כְּרָצוֹן, מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בַּנּוֹגֵחַ.

b13.he: יֵשׁ בַּנּוֹגֵחַ, שֶׁהַנּוֹגֵחַ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַכּוֹפֶר, מָה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בָּרוֹבֵעַ. הוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר רוֹבֵעַ, וְהוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר נוֹגֵחַ.

b14.he: וְהַאי תַּנָּא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ מֵהָכָא, דְּתַנְיָא: הָרוֹבֵעַ וְהַנִּרְבָּע (וְכוּלָּם) [וְכוּ׳]. הֵם כְּקָדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם עוֹבֵר לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן.

b15.he: וּצְרִיכִין מוּם קָבוּעַ לִפְדּוֹת עֲלֵיהֶן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי מׇשְׁחָתָם בָּהֶם מוּם בָּם״.

b16.he: מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא? חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהֵן אֲסוּרִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״כִּי מׇשְׁחָתָם בָּהֶם מוּם בָּם״, וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ׳הַשְׁחָתָה׳ — אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.

b17.he: דְּבַר עֶרְוָה — דִּכְתִיב ״כִּי הִשְׁחִית כׇּל בָּשָׂרוְגוֹ׳״, עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה — דִּכְתִיב ״פֶּן תַּשְׁחִיתוּן וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם פֶּסֶל תְּמוּנַת כׇּל סָמֶל״, כָּל שֶׁהַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן — דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בָּהֶן.

b18.he: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, ״מִן הַבְּהֵמָה מִן הַבָּקָר וּמִן הַצֹּאן״ מַאי דָרֵישׁ בְּהוּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ פְּרָט לְחוֹלֶה, זָקֵן, וּמְזוֹהָם.

b19.he: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא, דְּאַפְּקִינְהוּ לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי לְרוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע, חוֹלֶה, זָקֵן, וּמְזוֹהָם מְנָא לֵיהּ? נָפְקָא לֵיהּ ״מִן הַצֹּאן, מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן הָעִזִּים״. וּלְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אוֹרְחֵיהּ דִּקְרָא לְאִישְׁתַּעוֹיֵי הָכִי.

b20.he: אֵיזֶהוּ מוּקְצֶה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אֵין אָסוּר אֶלָּא מוּקְצֶה לְשֶׁבַע שְׁנַיִם.

b21.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא וַיֹּאמֶר [לוֹ ה׳] קַח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִיךָ וּפַר הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים״.

b22.he: וְהָתָם מוּקְצֶה בִּלְחוּד הֲוָה? נֶעֱבָד נָמֵי הֲוָה! אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: מוּקְצֶה לַעֲבוֹד, וְלֹא עֲבָדוּהוּ. רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם עֲבָדוּהוּ, וְחִידּוּשׁ הוּא, כִּדְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא: שְׁמֹנָה דְּבָרִים הִתִּירוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ לַיְלָה — חוּץ, וְלַיְלָה, וְזָרוּת,

messages.text: Continued from 27b, where chapter 5, כיצד מערימין · Keitzad Ma’arimin, ended.
Chapter 6 · כל האסורין · Kol HaAsurin: animals forbidden for the altar, and what happens when they are intermingled with animals that are permitted.
Mishna

With regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited, if they are intermingled with animals whose sacrifice is permitted, they prohibit the entire mixture of animals in any amount, regardless of the ratio of permitted to prohibited animals.

notes.dh: מתני' כל האסורין [לגבי מזבח] אוסרין בכל שהן
notes.he: אפי' נתערבו אחד באלף כולן אסורין למזבח אם אינו ניכר. וכולהו משכחת להו דאינן ניכרין אבל טרפה לא משכחת לה אלא כדמוקים לה במסכת זבחים בפרק כל הזבחים שנתערבו (זבחים דף עד:) כגון שנתערבה דרוסת הזאב בנקיבת הקוץ אי נמי בולד טרפה ואליבא דר"א דאמר לא יקרב:
notes.en: Mishna. All those forbidden [for the altar] prohibit in any amount: even if one was intermingled with a thousand, they are all forbidden for the altar, if it cannot be recognized. All of them can be found in a case where they cannot be recognized; but a tereifa can be found so only as it is explained in tractate Zevaḥim, in the chapter Kol HaZevaḥim SheNitarevu (Zevaḥim 74b): for example, an animal mauled by a wolf that was intermingled with one pierced by a thorn; or alternatively, with the offspring of a tereifa, according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says it may not be sacrificed.

notes.he: מתני' כל האסורין:
notes.en: Mishna: All those forbidden. [A heading only.]

notes.he: שאוסרין כל הבהמות שנתערבו בהן אפי' הן ריבוא:
notes.en: They prohibit for the altar in any amount: they prohibit all the animals with which they were intermingled, even if those are ten thousand.

messages.text: These are the animals whose sacrifice is prohibited: An animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality, and the set-aside, and one that was worshipped, and an animal that was given as payment to a prostitute or as the price of a dog, or an animal crossbred from a mixture of diverse kinds, or an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], or an animal born by caesarean section.

notes.he: כגון שניקב הוושט ואחר כך הבריא [העור] (העוף) עליו ואח"כ נתערבה באחרות:
notes.en: And the tereifa: for example, where the gullet was pierced and afterward the [skin] healed over it, and afterward it was intermingled with others. [A note in the printed edition asks why Rabbeinu does not explain as the Gemara does in Zevaḥim 74b, cited by Rashi here, since by his explanation the animal would be called a carcass and not a tereifa; it leaves this to be settled.]

messages.text: Which is the animal that is set-aside? It is an animal that is set aside for idol worship. The animal itself is prohibited, but that which is upon it, e.g., its jewelry and garments, is permitted to be sold in order to purchase an animal to be sacrificed.

And which is the animal that was worshipped? It is any animal that a person worships as an object of idol worship. In this case, the sacrifice of both the animal itself and an animal purchased using the money from the sale of that which is upon it is prohibited.
And the consumption of both this, the animal designated for idol worship, and that, the animal worshipped, is permitted.
Gemara

The Master said in the mishna, with regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited, that if they are intermingled with animals whose sacrifice is permitted, they prohibit the entire mixture in any amount. This teaches that they are not nullified by a majority. This is difficult, as we already learn this in a mishna:
messages.quote: they prohibit the entire mixture of animals in any amount

messages.text: All the sacrificial animals that were intermingled with an animal from which deriving benefit is prohibited, e.g., sin offerings that were disqualified and left to die, or if they were intermingled with an ox that is sentenced to be stoned, even if the ratio is one in ten thousand, deriving benefit from them all is prohibited and they must all die.

notes.he: באותן חמש חטאות שמתות:
notes.en: With sin offerings left to die: those five sin offerings that are left to die.

messages.text: And the use of the word “even” in the phrase: Even one in ten thousand, was difficult for us: What is it saying?
messages.quote: even if the ratio is one in ten thousand

messages.text: This word indicates that the novelty of the mishna’s ruling is that even if one permitted animal was intermingled with ten thousand prohibited animals they are all prohibited. Yet, this is less of a novelty than in the reverse case, since if in a situation where a minority of prohibited items became intermingled with a majority of permitted animals they are all prohibited, all the more so when the prohibited items are the majority.

notes.he: התם מאי אפי' דקאמר דהא קתני כל הזבחים שנתערבו בחטאות המתות דמשמע אחד מן הזבחים נתערב בהרבה חטאות המתות ואפי' אחד דהיתר ברבוא דאיסור כולן ימותו ומאי קאמר פשיטא לן דכ"ש דכי הוי איסורא יותר טפי (גבי איסור) פשיטא דימותו דהא איסור רובא:
notes.en: Gemara. And it was difficult for us: there, what is the “even” that it says? For it teaches: “All the offerings that were intermingled with sin offerings left to die,” which implies that one of the offerings was intermingled with many sin offerings left to die, and even one permitted animal in ten thousand forbidden ones, they all die. What is it saying? It is obvious to us; all the more so, when the forbidden are more numerous it is obvious that they die, since the forbidden are the majority.

notes.he: פשיטא דכי נתערב זבח אחד בחטאות מתות דכולן ימותו הואיל ורובן מתות:
notes.en: And it was difficult for us, what is it saying? It is obvious that when one offering was intermingled with sin offerings left to die, they all die, since most of them are left to die.

messages.text: And we explained that this is what the tanna is teaching: With regard to animals that are fit for the altar, if there was intermingled with them an animal from which deriving benefit is prohibited, e.g., one of the five sin offerings that are left to die if they are rendered disqualified, or if they were intermingled with an ox that is sentenced to be stoned, even if one prohibited animal was intermingled in ten thousand permitted animals, deriving benefit from them is prohibited and they must all die.

notes.he: התם דהכי קתני כל הזבחים שנתערב בהן אחד מחטאות המתות דמשמע דחדא חטאת נתערבה בזבחים כשהיו הרבה ואפילו אחת דאיסור ברבוא דהיתר כולן ימותו ולא בטיל חד בינייהו ולמה לי למיהדר ולמיתני הכא:
notes.en: And we answered: there, this is what it teaches: “All the offerings with which one of the sin offerings left to die was intermingled,” implying that one sin offering was intermingled among the offerings when they were many; and even one forbidden animal in ten thousand permitted ones, they all die, and the one is not nullified among them. So why do I need to go back and teach it here?

notes.he: אלא הכי קאמר כל הזבחים כשרים שנתערב בהן אחת מחטאת מת אפי' אחת בריבוא כולן ימותו דלא בטלה ברובא:
notes.en: Rather, this is what it says: All the fit offerings with which one of the sin offerings left to die was intermingled, even one in ten thousand, they all die, since it is not nullified by a majority.

messages.text: If so, the halakha of the mishna here was already taught in tractate Zevaḥim. Why, then, is its repetition necessary here?

It was necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that this halakha applies only there, with regard to the specific examples mentioned in the mishna in Zevaḥim, as the five sin offerings that are condemned to die and an ox that is sentenced to be stoned are items from which deriving benefit is prohibited.

notes.he: גבי חטאות המתות ושור הנסקל:
notes.en: There it is: with regard to sin offerings left to die and an ox to be stoned.

notes.he: ומשום הכי חשיבי ולא בטלי:
notes.en: That they are items forbidden for benefit: and for that reason they are significant and are not nullified.

notes.he: דהני חמש חטאות ושור הנסקל אסורין בהנאה:
notes.en: That applies to something forbidden for benefit: for these five sin offerings and the ox to be stoned are forbidden for benefit.

messages.text: But here, where the animals are not items from which deriving benefit is prohibited, but are merely prohibited to be sacrificed, you might say: Let them be nullified by a majority of permitted animals. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that even animals that are merely prohibited to be sacrificed prohibit other animals in any amount.

notes.he:
הני דמתני' רובע ונרבע דמותרין באכילה להדיוט דבהכי עסקינן שרבע או נרבע על פי עד אחד דאינה נסקלת בכך או שהבעלים הודו ומודה בקנס פטור אימא ליבטלו קמ"ל מתניתין:
ובזבחים (גרסי') תו ואי אשמועינן הא דתמורה ה"א הכא הוא דלגבוה מאיס ומשום הכי לא בטלי וירעו עד שיסתאבו ויאכלם ההדיוט אבל מילתא דלהדיוט נמי אסורה אימא ליבטל קמ"ל התם ימותו דאפי' לגבי הדיוט לא בטיל דאי בטיל לימא ירעו עד שיוממו ויפדו ויאכלם הדיוט:
notes.en: But: these of our mishna, an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, which are permitted to an ordinary person for eating. For we are dealing here with a case where it copulated or was the object of bestiality on the basis of one witness, so that it is not stoned on that account, or where the owners admitted it, and one who admits to [an act that carries] a fine is exempt. Say: let them be nullified. Our mishna teaches us [otherwise]. And in Zevaḥim we read further: and had it taught us that of Temurah, I would say it is here, since they are repulsive to the Most High, that they are not nullified, and they graze until they become blemished and an ordinary person eats them; but a thing forbidden to an ordinary person too, say it is nullified. It teaches us there: they die. For even with regard to an ordinary person it is not nullified, since if it were nullified, let it say: they graze until they become blemished, are redeemed, and an ordinary person eats them.

notes.dh: אבל הכא דלאו איסורי [הנאה] נינהו אימא ליבטלו ברובא
notes.he: ובפ' התערובת (זבחים עא:) קאמר ואי אשמועי' הכא ה"א דלהדיוט שריין קמ"ל הך דקתני התם ימותו ואפי' להדיוט אסירי:
notes.en: But here, where they are not [items forbidden for] benefit, say: let them be nullified by a majority. And in the chapter HaTa’arovet (Zevaḥim 71b) it says: and had it taught us only here, I would say that they are permitted to an ordinary person; it teaches us the one taught there, “they shall die,” and they are forbidden even to an ordinary person.

notes.dh: אבל כי מתערב מידי דלא אסור בהנאה
notes.he: כגון הני דמתניתין האתנן והמחיר והכלאים והטרפה לא להכי איצטריך מתניתין:
notes.en: But when something not forbidden for benefit is intermingled, such as those of our mishna, the prostitute’s payment, the price of a dog, the diverse kinds and the tereifa: for that our mishna was needed.

messages.text: But we already learn in a mishna the halakha of an animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality, and the other examples listed in the mishna here as well:

notes.he: התם בפרק התערובת (שם) משני אי מהתם מי קתני בכמה והכא קתני בכל שהוא והך דהתם איצטריך לאשמועינן תקנתא (והכא משני להו לעלמא):
notes.en: And the animal that copulated with a person and the one that was the object of bestiality: there, in the chapter HaTa’arovet (ibid.), it answers: from there, does it teach in what proportion? Here it teaches “in any amount.” And the one there was needed to teach us the remedy. (And here it answers them in another way.)

notes.he: והא נמי תנינא בסיפא דההיא דכל הזבחים נתערבו בהן רובע ונרבע ברובע על פי עד אחד או ע"פ הבעלים דאינו חייב מיתה קא מיירי ואינו אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: And this too we learned, in the latter clause of that [mishna], “All the offerings with which an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality was intermingled”: it speaks of an animal that copulated on the basis of one witness or on the basis of the owners, which is not liable to death and is not forbidden for benefit.

messages.text: If sacrificial animals were intermingled with an animal that copulated with a person, or with an animal that was the object of bestiality, or with the set-aside, with the animal worshipped, or with one of the other animals mentioned here, they shall graze until they become unfit for sacrifice and then sold, and from the money received the owner shall bring another offering with the monetary value of the higher-quality animal among them from the same species as the offering with which they were intermingled.

notes.he: תנינא התם בזבחים (ברובע) אחד מן הזבחים שנתערב ברובע ונרבע דחולין ירעו עד שיסתאבו וימכרו ויביא בדמי היפה שבהם קרבן מאותו המין - כלומר ממין אותו קרבן שנתערב בהן אם שלמים היו יביא בדמי יפה שבהן שלמים דיד הקדש על העליונה ואם עולה היתה יביא בדמי היפה עולה. אלמא שמעי' מהתם דלא בטלי ברובא:
notes.en: We learn there in Zevaḥim, [regarding] an animal that copulated: one of the offerings that was intermingled with a non-sacred animal that copulated with a person or was the object of bestiality: they graze until they become blemished and are sold, and he brings an offering of that same kind with the money of the best among them. That is, of the kind of the offering that was intermingled with them: if it was a peace offering, he brings a peace offering with the money of the best of them, since the hand of the Temple treasury is uppermost; and if it was a burnt offering, he brings a burnt offering with the money of the best. Evidently we learn from there that they are not nullified by a majority.

notes.dh: ימכרו כולן ויביא בדמי יפה שבהן מאותו מין
notes.he: כלומר אם נתערבו בעולות ובאשם ובשלמים ובחטאת ימכרו אותן ממין כדי לפטור חובתו אבל הן עצמן לא יקרבו אע"ג דרובע ונרבע לא אסור בהנאה אלמא אע"ג דאינן אסורין בהנאה לא בטלי ברובא:
notes.en: They are all sold, and he brings with the money of the best of them one of that same kind: that is, if they were intermingled with burnt offerings, a guilt offering, peace offerings or a sin offering, they are sold, and he brings with the money of the best [an offering] of that kind, to discharge his obligation; but they themselves are not sacrificed. Even though an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality is not forbidden for benefit: evidently, though they are not forbidden for benefit, they are not nullified by a majority. [Rendered with the correction the printed edition suggests.]

messages.text: This indicates that even in the case of an animal that may not be sacrificed, but from which one may derive benefit, it nevertheless renders other animals prohibited when intermingled.
I said this halakha before @Rav Shimi bar Ashi, and he said to me:

It was necessary for the mishna here to repeat this ruling. The reason is that one mishna is referring to a case where the previously fit animals became intermingled while they were still non-sacred, and their owners subsequently consecrated them. And the other mishna in Zevaḥim is referring to a situation where they became intermingled when they were already consecrated, as can be inferred from the opening phrase of that mishna: All the offerings (Zevaḥim 70b), which indicates that they are already offerings.

notes.he: מתני' דהכא מיירי בנתערבו כשהן חולין ואחר כך הקדישן וההיא דזבחים מיירי דנתערבו כשהן קדושים דהתם קתני כל הזבחים:
notes.en: One with non-sacred: the mishna here deals with where they were intermingled while non-sacred, and afterward he consecrated them; and the one in Zevaḥim deals with where they were intermingled when they were sacred, for there it teaches “All the offerings.”

notes.he: להכי איצטריך למימר הכא והכא דחדא בחולין מתניתין דהכא מיירי [שנתערבו בחולין והא כל הזבחים מיירי] שנתערבו בקדשים וצריכי דאי אשמעינן גבי קדשים משום הכי לא בטלי דמאיסי רובע ונרבע למיהוי קדשים אבל גבי חולין ליבטלו להכי איצטריך מתניתין:
notes.en: And Rav Shimi said to me: that is why it was necessary to state it here and there, for one is with non-sacred animals: the mishna here deals [with where they were intermingled with non-sacred animals, and the one of “All the offerings” deals] with where they were intermingled with sacred animals. And both are necessary: for had it taught us about sacred animals, [I would say] that is why they are not nullified, because an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality is repulsive to be made sacred; but with non-sacred animals, let them be nullified. For that our mishna was needed.

messages.text: And both mishnayot are necessary, as had the tanna taught us this halakha only with regard to sacrificial animals, one might say that the reason is because they are repulsive, i.e., when the sacrificial animals became intermingled with the other animals they were immediately disqualified from being sacrificed on the altar.

But with regard to animals that became intermingled when they were still non-sacred, at which stage they are not considered repulsive to the altar, as the altar does not yet have a claim to them, one might say: Let them be nullified in the mixture, after which all the animals could be dedicated to the altar. Therefore, the mishna here teaches that even if the animals became intermingled when they were non-sacred, nevertheless the entire mixture is prohibited.

notes.he:
הכא גבי חולין דלא מאיסי בשעת תערובות דלא שייך בהו חלק גבוה אימא ליבטלן וכי מקדיש להו קדשי שפיר דהא כבר איבטיל ליה איסור וליקרבו קמ"ל:
ובזבחים קפריך ניתני הא דתמורה ולא בעי הא דזבחים ומשני הכא תקנתא איצטריכא ליה להכי הדר תנא לה הכא בזבחים דהתם בתמורה תנא אוסרין בכל שהן ולא תנא תקנתא והכא תנא תקנתא ימכרו ויביא בדמי יפה שבהן מאותו המין:
notes.en: But: here, with non-sacred animals, which are not repulsive at the time of mixing, since the share of the Most High has no bearing on them, say they are nullified; and when he consecrates them they are properly sanctified, since the prohibition has already been nullified, and they may be sacrificed. It teaches us [otherwise]. And in Zevaḥim it asks: let it teach this one of Temurah, and that one of Zevaḥim would not be needed. And it answers: here [in Zevaḥim] the remedy was needed, which is why he taught it again here in Zevaḥim. For there in Temurah he taught “they prohibit in any amount” and did not teach the remedy, and here he taught the remedy: they are sold, and he brings with the money of the best of them one of that same kind.

notes.he: ל"א אי מן האי נתערבו בהן רובע ונרבע הוה אמינא הני מילי בקדשים:
notes.en: Another version: had it been [only] from that one, “an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality was intermingled with them,” I would have said that applies only to sacred animals.

notes.he: נתערבו בחולין אימא לא אסירא אלא ליבטלו אשמעינן הדא מתניתין דמיירי דנתערבו בחולין ולא בטלי:
notes.en: But with non-sacred: [if] they were intermingled with non-sacred animals, say it is not forbidden but they are nullified. This mishna teaches us, since it deals with where they were intermingled with non-sacred animals, that they are not nullified.

messages.text: But we also learn this halakha, that the entire mixture is prohibited with regard to non-sacred items, in another mishna:

notes.he: דאפילו בחולין ממש לא בטלי ברובא בעלי חיים וכל הנך דחשיבי:
notes.en: And with non-sacred too we learn: that even with actual non-sacred items, living animals and all these that are significant are not nullified by a majority.

notes.dh: ובחולין נמי תנינא ואלו אסורין ואוסרין בכל שהן יין נסך כו'
notes.he: דלא בטלי נמי בחולין אפי' הכי צריכא עלייהו מתניתין דאי מהתם הוה אמינא היינו טעמ' דלא בטלי ברוב חולין משום דאיסורי הנאה נינהו הנך כולהו יין נסך כו'. אבל הכא ליבטלי דלאו אסירי בהנאה להכי איצטריך מתניתין דלא בטלי:
notes.en: And with non-sacred too we learned: “And these are forbidden and prohibit in any amount: libation wine…,” that they are not nullified with non-sacred items either. Even so, our mishna is needed for them, for from there I would have said: this is the reason they are not nullified in a majority of non-sacred items, because all of these, libation wine and the rest, are forbidden for benefit; but here, let them be nullified, since they are not forbidden for benefit. That is why our mishna was needed: they are not nullified.

messages.text: And these are items that are prohibited in themselves and that deem other items prohibited if they became intermingled with them in any amount: Wine used for a libation in idol worship, and an object of idol worship, and birds for the purification of a leper (see Leviticus 14:1–6), and hides with a tear opposite the heart, a sign of the practice of sacrificing hearts of live animals for idol worship.

notes.he: מפרש במסכת ע"ז (דף לב.) שנוקבין כנגד הלב עגול בדרך אותו נקב הוציאו האימורין והקטירום לעבודת כוכבים ותקרובת עבודת כוכבים אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: And hides with a tear opposite the heart [levuvin]: it is explained in tractate Avoda Zara (32a) that they pierce a round hole opposite the heart, and through that hole they took out the sacrificial portions and burned them for idol worship; and an offering to idol worship is forbidden for benefit.

messages.text: And in addition, the shaved-off hair of a nazirite (Numbers 6:18); and a firstborn donkey (Exodus 13:13); and meat that was cooked in milk (Exodus 23:19; 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21), and an ox that is to be stoned; and a heifer whose neck is broken as part of the ritual performed when a murder victim’s body is found outside a town, and it is not known who caused his death (Deuteronomy 21:1–9); and non-sacred meat from an animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, and the scapegoat of Yom Kippur (Leviticus 16:7–10), all of these are prohibited in themselves and they deem mixtures prohibited in any amount.

notes.he: אסור בהנאה דבעי שילוח תחת הדוד:
notes.en: And the hair of a nazirite: it is forbidden for benefit, since it must be put under the pot [Numbers 6:18].

notes.he: חתיכת בשר שנתבשלה בחלב ושוב נתערבה באלף חתיכות כולן אסורות ואליבא דמאן דאמר בשר בחלב אסור בהנאה בשחיטת חולין בפרק כל הבשר (חולין דף קיד:):
notes.en: And meat in milk: a piece of meat that was cooked in milk and was then intermingled with a thousand pieces; they are all forbidden. This follows the one who says that meat in milk is forbidden for benefit, in Sheḥitat Ḥullin, in the chapter Kol HaBasar (Ḥullin 114b).

messages.text: Both mishnayot are necessary, as had the tanna taught us this halakha only there, in tractate Avoda Zara, one would have said that it is only in that case, where they are items from which deriving benefit is prohibited, that they are not nullified; but here, let them be nullified.

notes.he: בקדשים דתני איסורי הנאה כגון חטאות המתות ושור הנסקל ואיסורי אכילה כגון טרפה בהדי הדדי:
notes.en: What is different there: with sacrificial animals, where he teaches items forbidden for benefit, such as sin offerings left to die and an ox to be stoned, together with items forbidden for eating, such as a tereifa?

notes.he:
כלומר דגבי מסכת עבודת כוכבים הוי תערובת דחולין איפסיק ותני איסורי הנאה לחוד דקתני ואלו אסורין ואוסרין בכל שהן ואוסרין בהנאה יין נסך והדר תני בשיטה אחריתי ואלו דברים שאינן אסורין איסור הנאה חלב שחלבו עובד כוכבים ואין ישראל רואהו כו' מיסתברא קאי גבי מסכת עבודת כוכבים משום דבעי לפרושי איסורי דיין נסך דדמיין ליה דהם נמי אסורין בהנאה:
הכא נמי גבי זבחים דדמיין ליה דכולהו אסורין לגבוה:
notes.en: A mixture of non-sacred items, etc.: that is, in tractate Avoda Zara, with a mixture of non-sacred items, he broke off and taught items forbidden for benefit alone, as he teaches: “And these are forbidden and prohibit in any amount, and are forbidden for benefit: libation wine…,” and then teaches in a separate list: “And these are things that are not forbidden for benefit: milk that a gentile milked without a Jew watching him…” It stands to reason: he is in tractate Avoda Zara, and he wants to explain prohibitions that resemble libation wine, that they too are forbidden for benefit. Here too, with offerings, [he lists] those that resemble them, since all of them are forbidden to the Most High.

notes.he: כגון מוקצה ונעבד דלא בטלי בחולין אמאי איצטריך למיתני במתניתין הא תנא ליה חדא זימנא דתנן אלו אסורין ואוסרין בכל שהן יין נסך ועבודה זרה ועורות לבובין דלא בטלי בחולין אי מההיא הוה אמינא הני מילי איסור' לחודיהו דאסורין בהנאה כגון אלו דכולהו אסורין בהנאה כי נתערבו בחולין דלא בטלי אבל איסורין דאינן אסור בהנאה כגון אתנן ומחיר והכלאים והטרפה כי נתערבו בחולין אימא ליבטלן להכי איצטריך מתניתין דלא:
notes.en: And items forbidden for benefit, such as the set-aside and the worshipped animal, which are not nullified among non-sacred animals: why was it necessary to teach them in our mishna? He already taught it once, as we learned: “These are forbidden and prohibit in any amount: libation wine, an object of idol worship and hides with a tear opposite the heart,” that they are not nullified among non-sacred items. From that I would have said: that applies only to those prohibitions forbidden for benefit, like these, all of which are forbidden for benefit, that when intermingled with non-sacred items they are not nullified; but prohibitions not forbidden for benefit, such as the prostitute’s payment, the price of a dog, diverse kinds and the tereifa, when intermingled with non-sacred animals, say they are nullified. That is why our mishna was needed: [to teach] that they are not.

messages.text: And had the tanna taught us this halakha only here, I would have said that the mixture is prohibited in this case, as this mishna is dealing with offerings that have been rendered repulsive to the Most High.

But with regard to use by an ordinary person [hedyot], say: Let these other items from which deriving benefit is prohibited be nullified by a majority. Therefore, the mishna in Avoda Zara teaches us that even items not designated for use upon the altar render other items prohibited, and are not nullified by a majority.

notes.he: הא מתניתין לחוד הוה אמינא היינו טעמא דלא בטלי בהנך חולין דבעי להו לגבוה ומאיסי [אבל] להדיוט אימא אפי' איסורי הנאה ליבטלו ברוב להכי צריכא ואלו אסורין כו'. דאפי' להדיוט לא בטלי:
notes.en: And had it taught us only this mishna, I would have said: this is the reason they are not nullified among these non-sacred animals, because they are wanted for the Most High and are repulsive; [but] for an ordinary person, say even items forbidden for benefit are nullified by a majority. That is why “And these are forbidden…” was needed: that even for an ordinary person they are not nullified.

notes.he: ומאי שנא לענין אי איערוב בקדשים הא מתני' ומתני' דכל הזבחים שנתערבו בהן כו' קתני התם נמי טרפה בהדייהו דאסור באכילה דתני איסור הנאה ואיסור אכילה בהדי הדדי דמוקצה ונעבד היינו איסורי הנאה וטרפה לא אסירא בהנאה אלא באכילה ותני להו בהדדי:
notes.en: And what is different with regard to being intermingled with sacred animals? This mishna, and the mishna “All the offerings with which were intermingled…,” there too teaches the tereifa with them, which is forbidden for eating. For it teaches a prohibition of benefit and a prohibition of eating together: the set-aside and the worshipped animal are prohibitions of benefit, while the tereifa is forbidden not for benefit but only for eating, and he teaches them together.

notes.dh: ותערובת דחולין אפסק ותני איסורי הנאה לחוד
notes.he: כגון יין נסך וע"ז ועורות לבובין:
notes.en: And with a mixture of non-sacred items he broke off and taught prohibitions of benefit alone: such as libation wine, an object of idol worship and hides with a tear opposite the heart.

notes.he: דקתני סיפא ואלו אסורי' באכילה ומותר בהנאה חלב שחלבו עובד כוכבים ואין ישראל רואהו כו' [היינו טעמא דכי קאי במסכ' ע"ז משום דבעי לפרושי איסור' דיין נסך פריש גבי איסור דדמיין ליה כי קאי במתניתין כיון דבעי לפרושי מוקצה ונעבד ואתנן ומחיר דאסור לגבי מזבח מפרש נמי כל דאסור לגבי מזבח אפי' איסור כו':
notes.en: And a prohibition of eating alone: for it teaches in the latter clause, “And these are forbidden for eating and permitted for benefit: milk that a gentile milked without a Jew watching him…” [This is the reason: when he is in tractate Avoda Zara, since he wants to explain the prohibition of libation wine, he explains the prohibitions that resemble it. When he is in our mishna, since he wants to explain the set-aside, the worshipped animal, the prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog, which are forbidden for the altar, he explains also everything forbidden for the altar, even a prohibition…] [A note in the printed edition: that mishna, “These are forbidden for eating,” is in the second chapter [of Avoda Zara] and is not a latter clause at all, and the Gemara there (74a) gives the reason; Rabbeinu’s words require study.]

messages.text: Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom comment here on a further question that is not in our printed text: why does the mishna on offerings list animals forbidden for benefit together with those forbidden only for eating, while the mishna in Avoda Zara lists items forbidden for benefit separately? Their answer: each mishna gathers the prohibitions that resemble its subject.

messages.caption: Three earlier mishnayot, and why each one still leaves room for another.

messages.text: § The mishna’s list of disqualified animals includes an animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality. From where do we derive that these animals are prohibited as offerings to the Most High?

“You shall bring your offering from the cattle, even from the herd or from the flock.” The limitation indicated by the phrase “from the cattle” serves to exclude an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality from eligibility as an offering.
messages.lead: This is as the Sages taught with regard to the verse:

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אָדָם כִּי־יַקְרִיב מִכֶּם קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה מִן־הַבָּקָר וּמִן־הַצֹּאן תַּקְרִיבוּ אֶת־קׇרְבַּנְכֶם׃
verse.en:
Speak to the Israelite people, and say to them:
When any of you presents an offering of cattle to GOD: You shall choose your offering from the herd or from the flock.

notes.he: משמע ולא כל הבהמה:
notes.en: From the cattle: implying, and not all the cattle.

messages.text: That claim requires elucidation, as couldn’t this be derived through an a fortiori inference: And if a blemished animal, with which no transgression was committed, is disqualified from the altar, with regard to an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, with which a transgression was committed, is it not logical that they should be prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar?

notes.he: ולא צריך קרא:
notes.en: But isn’t it logical: and no verse is needed.

messages.text: The case of one who violates the prohibition of plowing with an ox and a donkey together (Deuteronomy 22:10) shall prove that the above claim is invalid. This is a case where a transgression was committed with the ox, and yet it is permitted to sacrifice it upon the altar.

notes.he: שמותר לגבוה אם הקדישו אחרי כן:
notes.en: Plowing with an ox and a donkey shall prove: for it is permitted to the Most High if one consecrated it afterward.

notes.dh: חורש בשור וחמור יוכיח שנעבדה בו עבירה ומותר למזבח
notes.he: כדדרשינן מאלה אי אתה מקריב אבל אתה מקריב קדשים שנתעבדה בהן עבירה:
notes.en: Plowing with an ox and a donkey shall prove, with which a transgression was committed and which is permitted for the altar: as we expound: “of any of these” [Leviticus 22:25] you may not sacrifice, but you may sacrifice sacrificial animals with which a transgression was committed.

messages.text: What is notable about the prohibition of one who plows with an ox and a donkey? It is notable in that one is not liable to die for this violation, and therefore it is logical that this ox is not prohibited to be sacrificed. Will you say the same with regard to the prohibitions of an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, where the person involved is liable to die? Therefore, the animals should be prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar.

This claim is indeed valid, and therefore you should retract from that which you cited as a refutation of the a fortiori inference. In other words, one can learn by a fortiori inference that an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality cannot be used as offerings. Nevertheless, this is applicable only to those animals with which a transgression was committed that was seen by two witnesses, and the transgressor was therefore liable to death by the court, as in this case the proof from one who plows with an ox and a donkey is invalid, as explained in the previous paragraph.

notes.he: דלאו פירכא היא מהאי טעמא:
notes.en: Take back what you brought: for it is not a refutation, for this reason [that plowing does not carry the death penalty].

notes.he: כלומר הרי יש לך להביא בדין זה אותו ששני עדים מעידין בו שרבע או שנרבע דהוא ודאי חייב מיתה ואסור לגבוה:
notes.en: Here is a case where a transgression was committed with them before two witnesses: that is, you may derive by this inference the animal about which two witnesses testify that it copulated or was the object of bestiality, since it is certainly liable to death and forbidden to the Most High.

notes.he: פרש"י לאו פירכא היא מהאי טעמא הרי שנתעבדה בה עבירה בשני עדים כלומר הרי יש לך להביא בדין זה אותו ששני עדים מעידין בו שרבע או שנרבע דהא ודאי חייב מיתה ואסור לגבוה על פי עד אחד או על פי הבעלים דליכא מיתה מנין לך דאסורין לגבוה אי לאו קרא עכ"ל וא"ת למה לי קל וחומר לרובע ונרבע ע"פ שני עדים תיפוק ליה ממשקה ישראל לקמן (תמורה דף כט.) דדרשינן מן המותר לישראל והאי הרי הוא אסור בהנאה וי"ל דאיצטריך היכא דשחטו והקריבו קודם שנגמר דינו דמותר בהנאה הוא כדאיתא בב"ק פרק ארבעה וחמשה (דף מא.) אי נמי יש לפרש טול מה שהבאת הרי שנעבדה בו עבירה בב' עדים ואפילו לקל וחומר לא צריכנא דבלאו הכי נמי ידע ביה שהוא אסור למזבח:
notes.en: Take back what you brought: Rashi explained: it is not a refutation, for this reason. Here is a case where a transgression was committed with it before two witnesses: that is, you may derive by this inference the animal about which two witnesses testify that it copulated or was the object of bestiality, since it is certainly liable to death and forbidden to the Most High. On the basis of one witness or of the owners, where there is no death penalty, from where would you know that they are forbidden to the Most High, were it not for the verse? End of his words. And if you will say: why do I need an a fortiori inference for an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality on the basis of two witnesses? Derive it from “from the well-watered pastures of Israel” below (Temurah 29a), where we expound: from what is permitted to Israel; and this one is forbidden for benefit. One can say: it is needed where one slaughtered and sacrificed it before its sentence was concluded, when it is permitted for benefit, as stated in Bava Kamma, chapter Arba’a VeḤamisha (41a). Alternatively, one can explain “take back what you brought”: here is a case where a transgression was committed with it before two witnesses, and I do not even need the a fortiori inference, since even without it one knows that it is forbidden for the altar.

notes.he: כלומר טול לך תשובה מראייה שהבאתה הרי שנעבדה בהן עבירה בשני עדים כלומר הרי מדין זה למדנו שנעבדה בהן עבירה בשני עדים. רובע ונרבע בעד א' לא למדנו להכי איצטריך מן הבהמה למעוטינהו דא"ר (ישמעאל) [שמעון] אני אדוננו לרובע ונרבע בעד אחד מדין ק"ו ומה בעל מום כו':
notes.en: Take back what you brought: that is, take an answer from the proof you brought. Here is a case where a transgression was committed with them before two witnesses: that is, from this inference we learned [the case] where a transgression was committed with them before two witnesses; an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality on the testimony of one witness we did not learn. That is why “from the cattle” was needed, to exclude them. For Rabbi (Yishmael) [Shimon] said: I infer an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality on one witness by an a fortiori inference: “And if a blemished animal…”

messages.text: From where is it derived that the same applies if a transgression was committed with them on the basis of the testimony of one witness or on the basis of the admission of the owners? For this purpose, the interpretation of the phrase “from the cattle” is necessary.

notes.dh: על פי עד אחד או על פי הבעלים
notes.he: דליכא מיתה מנין לך שאסור לגבוה אי לאו קרא:
notes.en: On the basis of one witness or on the basis of the owners: where there is no death penalty, from where would you know that it is forbidden to the Most High, were it not for the verse?

messages.text: I infer an a fortiori inference in the following manner: And if a blemished animal, concerning which the testimony of two witnesses does not disqualify it from being eaten by an ordinary person, and nevertheless the admission of one witness, i.e., the Sage who rules that its blemish disqualifies it for the altar, disqualifies it from sacrifice, with regard to an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, concerning which the admission of two witnesses disqualifies it from being eaten by an ordinary person, is it not logical that the admission of one witness should disqualify it from sacrifice?

notes.he: ולא צריך קרא:
notes.en: I infer it: and no verse is needed.

notes.he: דכיון דאמר חכם מום קבוע הוא פסול מהקרבה:
notes.en: The admission of one witness disqualifies it from sacrifice: for once a Sage has said that it is a permanent blemish, it is disqualified from sacrifice.

notes.he: שהרי בסקילה הוא:
notes.en: Disqualifies it from eating: for it is [subject to] stoning.

notes.he: כדאמרן בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין נאמן ישראל לומר בכור זה נתתי לכהן במומו:
notes.en: The admission of one witness disqualifies it from sacrifice: as we said in the chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin: an Israelite is deemed credible to say, “I gave this firstborn to a priest in its blemished state.”

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “From the cattle,” to exclude an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality from eligibility as offerings.

But why is this derivation necessary? This halakha was just inferred through an a fortiori inference, by Rabbi Shimon. The Gemara explains that in fact the halakha of an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality cannot be inferred by a fortiori inference according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon.

notes.he: ב' עדים פוסלין מאכילה דחייב מיתה הוא אינו דין שהעד עד אחד פוסל מהקרבה ת"ל מן הבהמה. הא למה לי קרא לרובע ונרבע ע"פ עד אחד:
notes.en: An animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality: two witnesses disqualify it from eating, since it is liable to death; is it not logical that one witness disqualifies it from sacrifice? The verse states: “From the cattle.” So why do I need a verse for an animal that copulated or was the object of bestiality on the testimony of one witness?

messages.text: One cannot derive the halakha of an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality by an a fortiori inference from a blemished animal, because one can say that the refutation of the a fortiori inference is found in the basic case itself, i.e., there is a problem with this comparison: What is notable about a blemished animal? It is notable in that its blemish is conspicuous, and it should perhaps be disqualified for this reason.

notes.dh: אמר רב אשי משום דאיכא למימר מעיקרא דדינא פירכא כו'
notes.he: ובת"כ קא אמר לה ר"ע להאי פירכא מה לבעל מום שכן מומו נגלה והיינו דקאמר הכא שכן מומו ניכר תימה אמאי לא קאמר אתנן ומחיר יוכיח דאין מומו ניכר ואסורין למזבח:
notes.en: Rav Ashi said: Because one can say that the refutation is in the basis of the inference, etc.: in the Torat Kohanim [Sifra], Rabbi Akiva says this refutation to him: what about a blemished animal, whose blemish is revealed? And that is what it says here, “whose blemish is conspicuous.” It is puzzling: why does he not say, a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog shall prove, whose blemish is not conspicuous and which are forbidden for the altar?

notes.he: מן דינא כדאמר ר' ישמעאל דמצי יליף מדינא אמר רב אשי איצטריך משום דאיכא למימר מעיקרא דדינא פירכא מה לבעל מום שכן מומו ניכר לכל העולם תאמר כו':
notes.en: But this is derived by inference, as Rabbi Yishmael [the daf has Rabbi Shimon] said, that it can be learned by inference. Rav Ashi said: it was needed, since one can say there is a refutation at the basis of the inference: what about a blemished animal, whose blemish is conspicuous to everyone? Will you say…

messages.text: Shall you say the same with regard to an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, whose blemish is not conspicuous? Since its blemish is not conspicuous, one can claim that it should be fit for the altar, despite the fact that a transgression was performed with it. Therefore the verse states: “From the cattle,” to exclude an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality from eligibility to be brought as an offering.

messages.caption: “From the cattle”: how far the a fortiori inference reaches, and why the verse is still needed.

messages.text: § The Gemara returns to discuss the baraita that interprets the verse: “You shall bring your offering from the cattle, even from the herd or from the flock” (Leviticus 1:2):
The phrase “from the herd” serves to exclude an animal that is worshipped.

Why is this verse necessary? Could this not be derived through an a fortiori inference: And if an animal given as payment to a prostitute for services rendered or given as payment for the price of a dog, which is more lenient in that their coating, i.e., the decorative part added to the animal, is permitted to be used on the altar, e.g., for fashioning golden plates for the altar, and yet they themselves are prohibited, then with regard to an animal that is worshipped, which is more stringent in that even its coating is prohibited, is it not logical that it itself should be prohibited to the Temple?

notes.he: אם סיככה עליו שום דבר לאחר שנתנו לה מותר הציפוי לבא לבית לעשות ריקועין למזבח דהתורה לא אסרה אלא גם שניהן ולא ציפוייהן:
notes.en: Their coatings: if one covered it with something after they gave it to her, the coating is permitted to come into the Temple, to make plates for the altar; for the Torah forbade only “even both of them,” and not their coatings.

notes.he: דכתיב לא תחמוד כסף וזהב עליהם וגו':
notes.en: A worshipped animal, whose coatings are forbidden: as it is written: “You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them…”

notes.dh: נעבד שעשאוהו עבודת כוכבים אינו דין שיהא הוא אסור לגבוה
notes.he: נהי דלהדיוט לא מיתסר דאין בעלי חיים אסורין כדאמרן טעמא לקמן אבל לגבוה מיהא אסור הואיל וציפויין אסור אפי' בהנאה להדיוט וקרא למה לי:
notes.en: A worshipped animal, which was made into an object of idol worship, is it not logical that it is itself forbidden to the Most High? Granted that it does not become forbidden to an ordinary person, since living creatures do not become forbidden, as we will give the reason below; but to the Most High at least it is forbidden, since its coatings are forbidden even for benefit to an ordinary person. So why do I need a verse?

notes.he: וה"ה דהוה מצי למעבד ק"ו כדאיתא פרק כל הצלמים (ע"ז מו:) ומה אתנן ומחיר שמותרים בתלוש להדיוט אסורים בבעלי חיים לגבוה נעבד שאסור בתלוש להדיוט אינו דין שאסור בבעלי חיים לגבוה והשתא לא שייך למימר או חילוף כדאמר הכא ובפרק כל הצלמים (גז"ש) לא עבד כי האי ק"ו לאסור אבני הר למזבח דאמר התם ומה אתנן דמותר בתלוש להדיוט אסור במחובר לגבוה נעבד כו' או חילוף ומה אתנן ומחיר שהם אסורין וציפוייהם מותרים והוה מצי למעבד האי ק"ו התם להתיר ציפוי הר אפי' למזבח:
notes.en: And if a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog, whose coatings are permitted: he could equally have made [another] a fortiori inference, as stated in the chapter Kol HaTzelamim (Avoda Zara 46b): and if a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog, which are permitted to an ordinary person in what is detached, are forbidden to the Most High as living creatures, then a worshipped animal, which is forbidden to an ordinary person in what is detached, is it not logical that it is forbidden to the Most High as a living creature? And then one could not say “or reverse it,” as is said here. And in the chapter Kol HaTzelamim he did not make such an a fortiori inference to forbid the stones of a mountain for the altar, for it says there: and if a prostitute’s payment, which is permitted to an ordinary person in what is detached, is forbidden to the Most High in what is attached [to the ground], a worshipped object…; or reverse it: and if a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog, which are forbidden, have their coatings permitted. And he could have made this a fortiori inference there, to permit the coating of a mountain, even for the altar.

notes.he: אם ציפה עליהן תקרה של כסף ושל זהב מותר ציפויין והן עצמן אסורין:
notes.en: And if a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog, whose coating is permitted: if one plated them with a covering of silver or gold, their coating is permitted, and they themselves are forbidden.

notes.he: לא תחמוד כסף וזהב עליהן וגו':
notes.en: A worshipped animal, whose coating is forbidden: “You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them…”

messages.text: Or perhaps one can reverse this reasoning: And if animals used as payment to a prostitute or as the price of a dog, whose halakhot are stringent, as they themselves are prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, and yet their coating is permitted, with regard to an animal that is worshipped, whose halakha is more lenient, as it is permitted to be sacrificed upon the altar, since the Torah does not explicitly state that it may not be sacrificed, certainly its coating should be permitted for use in the Temple.

notes.he: אי לא כתיב קרא איכא לחלופי דינא:
notes.en: Or reverse it: were the verse not written, one could reverse the law.

notes.he: דלא אשכחן דאסור:
notes.en: A worshipped animal, which is permitted: for we have not found that it is forbidden.

notes.he: וא"ת אמאי לא קאמר כל היכא דאיכא למיעבד לקולא ולחומרא עבדינן לחומרא והכי אמר פרק כל הצלמים (ע"ז מו:) וי"ל דגבי בעלי חיים אית לן למיעבד טפי לקולא דאין לנו לאסור בעלי חיים כיון דמצי למעבד ק"ו לקולא:
notes.en: Or reverse it, etc.: and if you will say: why does he not say that wherever one can argue toward leniency and toward stringency, we argue toward stringency? So it says in the chapter Kol HaTzelamim (Avoda Zara 46b). One can say: with living creatures we should rather argue toward leniency, since we should not forbid living creatures, given that an a fortiori inference toward leniency can be made.

notes.dh: נעבד שהוא מותר אינו דין שיהא ציפויו מותר
notes.he: ובפ' השוחט (חולין מ.) אמר התם דתקרובת דנעבד דבעלי חיים אסור דאמר הא דאמר להר הא דאמר לגדא דהר דתקרובתו אסור אלמא דמחמירין טפי בתקרובת דבעלי חיים מצפוי וגבי הר אמר איפכא דציפוי דהר קאמר התם פר' כל הצלמי' (ע"ז מה.) דאסור ותקרובתו מותר כדאמר פרק השוחט (חולין מ.) הא דאמר להר פי' אם שחט לשם הר תקרובתו מותר וי"ל דהא דאמר התם דציפוי דהר דאסור היינו הציפוי שהיה עליו בשעת השתחוואה וכי ה"ג ציפוי דבעלי חיים נמי אסור והא דקאמר הכא מותר היינו בציפוי הבאה לאחר השתחוואה אי נמי לפי המסקנא דאמר הכא דציפוי דנעבד אסור ניחא:
notes.en: A worshipped animal, which is permitted, is it not logical that its coating should be permitted: in the chapter HaShoḥet (Ḥullin 40a) it says that an offering to idol worship from a worshipped living creature is forbidden, for it says: this is where he said “to the mountain,” that is where he said “to the guardian spirit of the mountain,” whose offering is forbidden. Evidently we are more stringent with an offering of living creatures than with a coating. Yet with regard to a mountain it says the reverse: the coating of a mountain is forbidden, as stated in the chapter Kol HaTzelamim (Avoda Zara 45a), and its offering is permitted, as it says in the chapter HaShoḥet (Ḥullin 40a), “this is where he said to the mountain,” meaning that if he slaughtered for the sake of the mountain, its offering is permitted. One can say: what it says there, that the coating of a mountain is forbidden, means the coating that was on it at the time of the bowing down, and so too the coating of living creatures is then forbidden; what it says here, that it is permitted, refers to a coating that came after the bowing down. Alternatively, according to the conclusion here, that the coating of a worshipped animal is forbidden, it is well.

notes.dh: אינו דין שהוא אסור למזבח או חילוף
notes.he: כלומר אני אומר חילוף הדבר להתיר ומה אתנן ומחיר שהן אסורין בפירוש מן התורה ציפויין מותר נעבד שהוא מותר למזבח שלא מצינו שאסור בפירוש מן התורה אינו דין שציפויו מותר:
notes.en: Is it not logical that it is forbidden for the altar? Or reverse it: that is, I say the matter is reversed, to permit. And if a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog, which are forbidden explicitly by the Torah, have their coating permitted, then a worshipped animal, which is permitted for the altar, since we have not found it explicitly forbidden by the Torah, is it not logical that its coating is permitted?

messages.text: If so, you have nullified the requirement of the verse: “The graven images of their gods shall you burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it to you”. This verse is clearly referring to the coatings of items worshipped, in addition to the idols themselves.

verse.he: פְּסִילֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ לֹא־תַחְמֹד כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב עֲלֵיהֶם וְלָקַחְתָּ לָךְ פֶּן תִּוָּקֵשׁ בּוֹ כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא׃
verse.en: You shall consign the images of their gods to the fire; you shall not covet the silver and gold on them and keep it for yourselves, lest you be ensnared thereby; for that is abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.dh: הכי קאמר א"כ ביטלת לא תחמוד כו'
notes.he: הלכך ליכא למימר או חילוף הואיל ומדינא אתיא דאסור נעבד לגבוה לא צריך קרא דקאמר:
notes.en: This is what it says: if so, you have nullified “You shall not covet…” Therefore one cannot say “or reverse it”; and since it follows from the inference that a worshipped animal is forbidden to the Most High, the verse he cited is not needed.

notes.he: אמר לו בעל הדין ראשון אם כן לדבריך שאתה רוצה להתיר ציפוי דנעבד ביטלת לא תחמוד כסף וזהב עליהן וגו':
notes.en: The first disputant said to him: if so, according to your words, that you wish to permit the coating of a worshipped animal, you have nullified “You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them…”

messages.text: I shall establish the clause: “You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them,” as referring to a coating of an entity that is not alive. But with regard to the coating of an entity that is alive, since such entities themselves are permitted to be sacrificed on the altar, one might have thought that even its coating should be permitted.

notes.he: הלכך איכא למימר או חילוף והואיל והוא מותר אפילו לגבוה ציפויין מותר:
notes.en: I will establish it, etc.: therefore one can say “or reverse it”; and since it is permitted even to the Most High, its coatings are permitted.

notes.dh: אמר לך אני אקיימנה בדבר שאין בו רוח חיים
notes.he: כלומר נעבד שאין בו רוח חיים ציפויין אסור אבל נעבד דבר שיש בו רוח חיים כגון בהמה הואיל והיא מותר כדאמרן יהא ציפוי מותר להכי איצטריך מן הבקר להוציא את הנעבד. האי לישנא אחרינא אימא אשכחן כו' לא אמר לן רבי:
notes.en: He said to you: I will establish it with regard to an entity that has no breath of life. That is, a worshipped entity with no breath of life: its coating is forbidden; but a worshipped entity with the breath of life, such as an animal, since it is permitted, as we said, let its coating be permitted. That is why “from the herd” was needed, to exclude the worshipped animal. This other version, “say, we found…,” my teacher did not tell us.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “From the herd,” to exclude an animal that is worshipped. Once it has been derived that a worshipped living creature is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, it follows that its coating is also prohibited.

notes.dh: ת"ל מן הבקר ולא כל הבקר להוציא את הנעבד
notes.he: דאסור לגבוה וכיון דאסור לגבוה ציפויין אסור אף להדיוט דקרינא ביה לא תחמוד וגו':
notes.en: The verse states “from the herd,” and not all the herd, to exclude the worshipped animal: that it is forbidden to the Most High; and since it is forbidden to the Most High, its coatings are forbidden even to an ordinary person, for we apply to it “You shall not covet…”

notes.dh: תלמוד לומר מן הבקר להוציא הנעבד
notes.he: פירש רש"י דאסור לגבוה וכיון דאסור לגבוה ציפויו אסור אף להדיוט דקרינא ביה כסף וזהב עליהם לשון רש"י והדין עמו דפי' כן דאין לומר דלפי האי מיעוטא נמי דציפוי מותר להדיוט ולא תחמוד כסף וזהב עליהם מוקמינן ליה בשאין בו רוח חיים אבל בבעלי חיים מותר לגבוה דמדקפריך בסמוך טעמא דמעטיה קרא משמע דפשיטא ליה דאחר דמעטיה קרא כל ציפוי דנעבד אסור בבעלי חיים וכן משמע הסוגיא:
notes.en: The verse states “from the herd,” to exclude the worshipped animal: Rashi explained: that it is forbidden to the Most High, and since it is forbidden to the Most High, its coating is forbidden even to an ordinary person, for we apply to it “the silver or the gold that is on them.” These are Rashi’s words. And he was right to explain it so. For one cannot say that even according to this exclusion the coating is permitted to an ordinary person, and that we establish “you shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them” for what has no breath of life, while with living creatures it is permitted to the Most High. For since it asks just below, “the reason is that the verse excluded it,” it implies that it is obvious to him that once the verse excluded it, every coating of a worshipped living creature is forbidden. And so the passage implies.

messages.text: According to this explanation, the only reason that the coating of an animal that was worshipped is prohibited is that the verse excluded it, from which it may be inferred that if the verse had not excluded it, then the coating would be permitted. But isn’t it written that idolatry must be entirely eradicated: “And you shall break down their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and burn their Asherim with fire; and you shall hew down the graven images of their gods; and you shall destroy their name out of that place”. This teaches that not only must the idols themselves be destroyed, but also everything made in their name, including their coating, must be destroyed.

verse.he: וְנִתַּצְתֶּם אֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָם וְשִׁבַּרְתֶּם אֶת־מַצֵּבֹתָם וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ וּפְסִילֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶם תְּגַדֵּעוּן וְאִבַּדְתֶּם אֶת־שְׁמָם מִן־הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא׃
verse.en: Tear down their altars, smash their pillars, put their sacred posts to the fire, and cut down the images of their gods, obliterating their name from that site.

notes.he: והא כתיב ואבדתם את שמם כל העשוי לשמם:
notes.en: But isn’t it written: “And you shall destroy their name”: everything made for their sake.

messages.text: That phrase: “And you shall destroy their name,” does not teach this halakha. Rather, it comes to teach that one should give a derogatory nickname to idol worship, and not call them by their original names.
messages.quote: and you shall destroy their name

notes.he: האי ואבדתם את שמם לא אתא אלא לחייב:
notes.en: This “and you shall destroy their name” comes only to obligate [us]

messages.text: For example, if idolaters refer to a place of worship as: House of Elevation [beit galya], one calls it: House of Annihilation [beit karya]. If the place is called: Face of the Molekh [penei haMolekh], one calls it: Face of a Dog [penei kelev], and if it is called: All-seeing Eye [ein kol], one calls it: Eye of a Thorn [ein kotz].

notes.he: לשון גובה (ל"א) בית כלייא כמו כלוא כליון. ל"א בית כריא בית הכסא לשון כרו שוחה (ירמיהו יח):
notes.en: Beit galya: a term of height. (Another version:) beit kalya, like kelua, destruction. Another version: beit karya, a privy, from the term “they dug [karu] a pit” (Jeremiah 18).

notes.dh: לכנות להם שם לגנאי כגון ע"ז שקרויה] בית גליא
notes.he: כלומר גלויה ומפורסמת לכל:
notes.en: to give them a derogatory name, as idol worship that is called Beit Galya: that is, revealed and known to all.

notes.he: כלומר לכלות עיניהם:
notes.en: One calls it Beit Kalya: that is, for their eyes to be consumed. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads beit kalya, where our text has beit karya.]

messages.text: The baraita teaches that the phrase “from the cattle” (Leviticus 1:2) excludes an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality from eligibility to be brought as an offering, while the phrase “from the herd” excludes an animal worshipped as an object of idolatry. But perhaps I can reverse these derivations, as follows: The phrase “from the cattle” serves to exclude an animal that was worshipped, and the phrase “from the herd” serves to exclude an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality.

There, with regard to the phrase “from the cattle [behema],” the derivation is based on the context of the verse, as the halakha of an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality is written with regard to a domesticated animal: “And if a man lie with a beast [behema], he shall surely be put to death, and you shall slay the beast. And if a woman approach any beast [behema] and lie down with it, you shall kill the woman, and the beast”.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן שְׁכׇבְתּוֹ בִּבְהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה תַּהֲרֹגוּ׃ וְאִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר תִּקְרַב אֶל־כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה לְרִבְעָהֿ אֹתָהּ וְהָרַגְתָּ אֶת־הָאִשָּׁה וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָתוּ דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with an animal, he shall be put to death; and you shall kill the animal. If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal; they shall be put to death—and the bloodguilt is theirs.

notes.he: דאשכחן דברובע נסיב קרא בהמה ובדבר עבודת כוכבים נסיב לשון בקר:
notes.en: From the context of the verse: for we find that with regard to bestiality the verse uses “animal” [behema], and with regard to a matter of idol worship it uses the term “herd” [bakar].

messages.text: By contrast, the prohibition of idol worship is written with regard to an animal of the herd: “They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped a molten image. Thus they exchanged their glory for the likeness of an ox that eats grass”.

verse.he: יַעֲשׂוּ־עֵגֶל בְּחֹרֵב וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְמַסֵּכָה׃ וַיָּמִירוּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדָם בְּתַבְנִית שׁוֹר אֹכֵל עֵשֶׂב׃
verse.en:
They made a calf at Horeb
and bowed down to a molten image. They exchanged their glory
for the image of a bull that feeds on grass.

messages.text: § The baraita further teaches:

The phrase “from the flock” (Leviticus 1:2) serves to exclude an animal set aside for idol worship, while the conjunction “or” at the beginning of the phrase “or from the flock” (Leviticus 1:2) serves to exclude an animal that gored and killed a person.

notes.he: שהקצוהו לצורך תקרובת עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: Set-aside: which they set aside for use as an offering to idol worship.

notes.he: שהמית את האדם בעד אחד דלא מיסתקיל:
notes.en: The one that gored: that killed a person, on the testimony of one witness, so that it is not stoned.

messages.text: If it is stated that an animal that copulated with a person is disqualified as a sacrifice, why is it stated that an animal that gored is disqualified? And if it is stated that an animal that gored is disqualified, why is it stated that an animal that copulated with a person is disqualified? How do the transgressions differ?

notes.he: דאסור להקרבה והלא שניהם שוין דאם היו ב' עדים בדבר שניהם נסקלין:
notes.en: If it is stated that it copulated: that it is forbidden for sacrifice. For aren’t both equal? If there were two witnesses to the matter, both are stoned.

notes.dh: אם אמר נוגח למה הוצרך להוציא רובע
notes.he: והלא שניהן במיתה וילמד זה מזה מפני שיש כו':
notes.en: If it stated an animal that gored, why was it necessary to exclude one that copulated? Are not both [subject to] death, so let one be learned from the other? Because there is…

messages.text: It is because there is a stringency pertaining to an animal that copulated with a person that does not pertain to one that gored, and vice versa. There is a stringency pertaining to an animal that copulated with a person, as with regard to an animal that copulated with a person, the Torah renders an animal that is a victim of forced copulation like one that acted willfully, which is not so with regard to an animal that gored, which is exempt if others induced it to gore.

notes.he: לא עשה בו אונס כרצון לענין סקילה דתנן (ב"ק דף לט.) שור האיצטדין אינו חייב סקילה שנאמר שור כי יגח ולא שיגיחוהו אחרים:
notes.en: One that gored: [the Torah] did not make forced like willing with regard to stoning, as we learned (Bava Kamma 39a): a stadium ox is not liable to stoning, as it is stated: “If an ox gore,” and not that others make it gore.

notes.he: שאילו רבע בהמה לאונסה חייבת מיתה כרצון מה שאין כן בנוגח כדתנן שור האיצטדין אינו חייב מיתה שנאמר כי יגח שור ולא שיגיחוהו:
notes.en: That with an animal that copulated they made the forced like the willing: for if [a person] copulated with an animal by force, it is liable to death as if it were willing; which is not so with one that gored, as we learned: a stadium ox is not liable to death, as it is stated, “if an ox gore,” and not that others make it gore.

messages.text: By contrast, there is a stringency pertaining to an animal that gored, as with regard to an animal that gored, its owner pays a ransom; which is not so with regard to the owner of an animal that copulated with a person. Therefore, the Torah had to state that an animal that copulated with a person is disqualified, and it also had to state that an animal that gored is disqualified.

notes.he: אע"פ שהשור נסקל:
notes.en: Pays the ransom for it: even though the ox is stoned.

notes.he: משלם את הכופר לאחר מיתה כדכתיב סקול יסקל השור וגו' אם כופר יושת עליו וגו' וזה שייך לעיל טעמא דמעטיה קרא מן הבקר להוציא את הנעבד הא לאו הכי ציפוי מותר:
notes.en: It pays the ransom after [the ox’s] death, as it is written: “The ox shall be stoned… If a ransom be laid on him…” And this belongs above: “The reason is that the verse excluded it, ‘from the herd,’ to exclude the worshipped animal; but if not, the coating would be permitted.”

messages.text: § The baraita teaches that the prohibition of sacrificing an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality on the altar is derived from the phrase “from the cattle.” And this tanna cites that halakha from here, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דרובע ונרבע אסורין לגבוה:
notes.en: And this tanna derives it from here: that an animal that copulated with a person and one that was the object of bestiality are forbidden to the Most High.

notes.dh: והאי תנא מייתי לה מהכא דתניא כו'
notes.he: תימה דהכא משמע דר"ש לית ליה האי דרשא דכי משחתם דהא מפיק ליה לעיל מקרא אחרינא מדאמר אם נאמר נוגח למה נאמר רובע משמע דדריש ליה ממן הבקר ובפרק אין מעמידין (ע"ז כג:) קאמר ר"ש לענין רביעה דפסולה דכתיב כי משחתם בהם מום בם אלמא משמע דדריש ליה ממשחתם וי"ל דהא דקאמר לר"ש לעיל אם נאמר נוגח לדבריו דת"ק קא א"ל דמפיק ליה מן הבקר וליה לא סבירא ליה דדריש ליה מכי משחתם:
notes.en: And this tanna derives it from here, as it is taught, etc.: it is puzzling, for here it implies that Rabbi Shimon does not hold this exposition of “because their corruption is in them,” since above he derives it from another verse, as he says: “If it is stated that it gored, why is it stated that it copulated?”, implying that he expounds it from “from the herd.” Yet in the chapter Ein Ma’amidin (Avoda Zara 23b) Rabbi Shimon says with regard to bestiality that it is disqualified, as it is written: “because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them,” evidently implying that he expounds it from “their corruption.” One can say: what he says above for Rabbi Shimon, “If it is stated that it gored,” he says to him according to the words of the first tanna, who derives it from “from the herd”; but he himself does not hold so, for he expounds it from “because their corruption.”

notes.he: [גבי בהמה כתיב ואשה לא תעמוד לפני בהמה לרבעה הילכך מסתבר דבהמה אתי למעוטי נרבע ובקר למעוטי נעבד דכתיב וימירו את כבודם בתבנית שור דהיינו בקר] (ע"כ שייך לעיל) והדין תנא ממעט להו מהכא לנרבע ומוקצה ונעבד כו':
notes.en: [With regard to a domesticated animal [behema] it is written: “Neither shall any woman stand before an animal to lie down with it” [Leviticus 18:23]; therefore it stands to reason that “from the cattle” [behema] comes to exclude the animal that was the object of bestiality, and “herd” to exclude the worshipped animal, as it is written: “Thus they exchanged their glory for the likeness of an ox,” which is herd.] (Until here it belongs above.) And this tanna excludes them from here: the one that was the object of bestiality, the set-aside and the worshipped animal…

messages.text: With regard to an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality that were consecrated, they are considered like sacrificial animals whose temporary blemish preceded their consecration.

notes.he: שרוע וקלוט ל"ג:
notes.en: “An animal with an extended limb and one with uncloven hooves”: we do not read [these words in this baraita].

notes.he: אם הקדישן הרי הן כקדשים שקדם מום עובר להקדישן דכל הני לאו גבי מומין כתיבי וצריכי מום קבוע לפדות עליהן כדין קדשים שקדם מום עובר להקדשן:
notes.en: As the Sages taught: the one that was the object of bestiality and the set-aside, etc.: if he consecrated them, they are like sacrificial animals whose temporary blemish preceded their consecration, since none of these is written among the blemishes; and they need a permanent blemish to be redeemed, like the law of sacrificial animals whose temporary blemish preceded their consecration.

messages.text: And animals with a temporary blemish cannot be sacrificed at present, nor can they be redeemed. Rather, they require a permanent blemish for one to redeem them on account of that blemish, as it is stated with regard to the disqualification of blemished animals from the altar: “Neither from the hand of a foreigner shall you offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them; they shall not be accepted for you”.

verse.he: וּמִיַּד בֶּן־נֵכָר לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ אֶת־לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מִכׇּל־אֵלֶּה כִּי מׇשְׁחָתָם בָּהֶם מוּם בָּם לֹא יֵרָצוּ לָכֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: nor shall you accept such [animals] from a foreigner for offering as food for your God, for they are mutilated, they have a defect; they shall not be accepted in your favor.

messages.text: What is the biblical derivation here? How is this verse relevant to an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality? The baraita is incomplete and this is what it is teaching: From where is it derived that an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality are prohibited to be sacrificed? The verse states: “Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them,”

notes.he: להקרבה:
notes.en: That they are forbidden: for sacrifice.

notes.dh: ומנין שאסורים לגבי מזבח דכת' כי משחתם ואמר מר כו'
notes.he: נרבע ומוקצה ונעבד מימעטי מהשחתה [דהיינו] ערוה וע"ז. ואתנן ומחיר כתיב בקראי דאסור למזבח:
notes.en: And from where that they are forbidden for the altar? As it is written: “because their corruption,” and the Master said, etc.: the one that was the object of bestiality, the set-aside and the worshipped animal are excluded by “corruption,” [which means] sexual immorality and idol worship. And the prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog are written explicitly in verses as forbidden for the altar.

messages.text: Anywhere that the term corruption is stated, it is a reference only to a matter of sexual immorality and idol worship.
messages.lead: and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught a principle with regard to the derivation of verses:

notes.he: רובע ונרבע דבר ערוה. מוקצה ונעבד דבר עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: An animal that copulated with a person and one that was the object of bestiality: a matter of sexual immorality. The set-aside and the worshipped animal: a matter of idol worship.

messages.text: Corruption refers to a matter of sexual immorality, as it is written with regard to the generation of the flood, which was steeped in sexual immorality: “And God saw the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth”.

verse.he: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאָרֶץ וְהִנֵּה נִשְׁחָתָה כִּי־הִשְׁחִית כׇּל־בָּשָׂר אֶת־דַּרְכּוֹ עַל־הָאָרֶץ׃ {ס}
verse.en: When God saw how corrupt the earth was, for all flesh had corrupted its ways on earth,

messages.text: Corruption also refers to idol worship, as it is written: “Lest you deal corruptly, and make you a graven image even the form of any figure”.

verse.he: פֶּן־תַּשְׁחִתוּן וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם פֶּסֶל תְּמוּנַת כׇּל־סָמֶל תַּבְנִית זָכָר אוֹ נְקֵבָה׃
verse.en: not to act wickedly and make for yourselves a sculptured image in any likeness whatever: the form of a man or a woman,

messages.text: Since the term corruption is also used with regard to blemished animals, the following may be derived: In any case in which a blemish disqualifies an animal from the altar, a matter of sexual immorality, such as an animal that copulated with a person or an animal that was the object of bestiality, or their use as an object of idol worship, also disqualifies them.

notes.dh: כל שהמום פוסל בו דבר ערוה ועבודת כוכבים פוסלין בו
notes.he: צריך עיון מאי קאמר הא דרשינן שפיר רובע ונרבע מכי משחתם:
notes.en: Any case in which a blemish disqualifies, sexual immorality and idol worship disqualify: this requires study. What is it saying? We have properly expounded the animal that copulated and the one that was the object of bestiality from “because their corruption.”

notes.he: כגון בעופות לא משמע ליה האי דאמר מר כל שהמום כו':
notes.en: And where a blemish does not disqualify, such as with birds: he does not understand [these] from what the Master said, “any case in which a blemish…” [A note in the printed edition: it seems one should read that from this verse we do not learn about birds; but nonetheless an animal that copulated and one worshipped are disqualified among birds too, as in Ḥullin 23 and Zevaḥim 85a.]

messages.text: And according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, who says that the disqualifications of an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, the set-aside, and the worshipped animal, are derived from the case of blemished animals, what does he derive from the verse: “From the cattle, even from the herd or from the flock” (Leviticus 1:2), which is the source of these disqualifications according to the earlier baraita? He requires these three terms to exclude sick, old, and filthy animals, which may not be sacrificed.

notes.he: שמוציא זיעה ומסריח:
notes.en: Filthy: that gives off sweat and smells foul.
