messages.text: And the first tanna, who derives from these verses the halakha of an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality, from where does he derive the ruling that sick, the old, and filthy are disqualified from being sacrificed on the altar? He derives it from the verse: “And if his offering be of the flock, whether of the sheep or of the goats”.

verse.he: וְאִם־מִן־הַצֹּאן קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן־הַכְּשָׂבִים אוֹ מִן־הָעִזִּים לְעֹלָה זָכָר תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ׃
verse.en: If your offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, of sheep or of goats, you shall make your offering a male without blemish.

notes.he: קרא אחרינא אם מן הצאן קרבנו מן הכבשים או מן העזים לעולה:
notes.en: From the sheep, etc.: another verse: “And if his offering be of the flock, of the sheep or of the goats, for a burnt offering.”

notes.he: וי"ו דומן העזים הרי אלו ג' מיעוטי:
notes.en: From the sheep, from the goats: with the vav of “and from the goats,” these are three exclusions.

messages.text: And according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, that these halakhot are not derived from that verse, it is because it is the manner of the verse to say this, i.e., to state the general category of flock before specifying sheep and goats.

notes.he: ולאו לדרש' אתאן. [המוקצה לצורך ע"ז הוא אסור למזבח וציפוי שעליו מותר בהנאה דעדיין לא נעבד. וזה וזה בין מוקצה ובין נעבד מותר באכילה]:
notes.en: It is the manner of the verse to speak so: and they do not come for exposition. [The set-aside for idol worship is forbidden for the altar, and the coating on it is permitted for benefit, since it has not yet been worshipped. And both this and that, both the set-aside and the worshipped animal, are permitted for eating.]

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: Which is the animal that is set-aside? It is an animal that is set aside for idol worship.
messages.quote: Which is the animal that is set-aside? It is an animal that is set aside for idol worship.

messages.text: Only an animal that has been set aside for seven years is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, i.e., one that is set aside to be used for idol worship at the end of seven years.

notes.he: שהוקצה עד לז' שנים ובסוף ז' שנים יקריבוהו לעבודת כוכבים דהכי הוי מוקצה:
notes.en: For seven years: that was set aside for seven years, and at the end of seven years they would sacrifice it to idol worship; for this is what set-aside is.

notes.he: אין מוקצה אסור למזבח אלא אותו שעבר שבע שנים שהקצוהו לעבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: The set-aside is forbidden for the altar only [if] it is one that has passed seven years since they set it aside for idol worship.

messages.text: As it is stated with regard to Gideon: “And it came to pass the same night, that the Lord said to him: Take your father’s bullock, and the second bullock of seven years, and throw down the altar of Baal that your father has, and cut down the Asherah that is by it; and build an altar to the Lord your God…and take the second bullock, and sacrifice a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you shall cut down” (Judges 6:25–26). This indicates that it was common practice to prepare a bullock for seven years as an object of idol worship.

verse.he: וַיְהִי בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ יְהֹוָה קַח אֶת־פַּר־הַשּׁוֹר אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִיךָ וּפַר הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים וְהָרַסְתָּ אֶת־מִזְבַּח הַבַּעַל אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִיךָ וְאֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרָה אֲשֶׁר־עָלָיו תִּכְרֹת׃
verse.en: That night GOD said to him: “Take the young bull belonging to your father and another bull seven years old; pull down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the sacred post that is beside it.

notes.he: שפיטמוהו שבע שנים אלמא הכי אורחייהו למעבד:
notes.en: And the bullock of seven years: that they fattened for seven years. Evidently that is their way of doing it.

notes.dh: שנאמר ויהי בלילה ההוא ויאמר לו ה' קח את פר השור אשר לאביך ופר השני שבע שנים
notes.he: האי השני היינו מפוטם ז' שנים לעבודת כוכבים כגון והבקר והמשנים:
notes.en: As it is stated: “And it came to pass that night, that the Lord said to him: Take your father’s bullock, and the second bullock of seven years”: this “second” [sheni] means fattened for seven years for idol worship, as in “and the cattle and the fatlings [mishnim].”

messages.text: And there, was that bullock prohibited merely as set-aside? It was also actually worshipped.

notes.he: לא ידענא מהיכן נפקא:
notes.en: It was also worshipped: I do not know where this is derived from.

notes.dh: ל"א אין איסור מוקצה אלא ז' שנים
notes.he: ומז' שנים ואילך לא הוי מוקצה דתו לא מקרבי ליה דכתיב ופר שני שבע שנים אלמא דמשום דחלפין עליה ז' שנים אישתרי:
notes.en: Another version: the prohibition of set-aside applies only for seven years, and from seven years on it is not set-aside, since they no longer sacrifice it, as it is written: “and the second bullock of seven years.” Evidently, because seven years had passed over it, it became permitted.

notes.he: והדין מוקצה לחודיה הוא והא נעבד נמי הוא דקרוי הוא בעל דכת' והרסת את מזבח הבעל העשוי לצורך אותו פר שהוא בעל:
notes.en: And this one was only set-aside? But it was also worshipped, for it is called Baal, as it is written: “and throw down the altar of Baal,” [the altar] made for that bull, which is a Baal.

messages.text: This bullock was set aside to be worshipped, but in practice, they did not worship it.
Actually, they did worship it, and therefore it should have been prohibited as idolatry. But this case is a novelty, in accordance with a statement of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana.

notes.he: אלא מההוא לא גמרי מידי דחידוש הוא:
notes.en: Actually, they worshipped it: but we learn nothing from that case, since it is a novelty.

messages.text: Eight prohibited matters were permitted to Gideon on that night when he destroyed his father’s idolatry (see Judges, chapter 6): The prohibition against slaughtering sacrificial animals outside the Tabernacle; and the prohibition against sacrificing offerings at night; and the prohibition of non-priests performing the service, as Gideon was not a priest;

notes.he: שחוטי חוץ:
notes.en: Outside: slaughtering outside [the Temple].

notes.he: דהכי כתיב ויעש לילה:
notes.en: And at night he sacrificed: for so it is written: “he did it by night.”

notes.he: וחידוש הוא כל אותו מעשה דגדעון לפי שחוץ (לארץ) היה [ולילה הוי] (היה ולא לה) דלא הוי זמן הקרבה וזרות דלא הוי כהן וכלי שרת הקדיש מכלי אשירה היו:
notes.en: And that whole deed of Gideon is a novelty: for it was outside, [and it was night,] which is not a time for sacrifice; and by a non-priest, since he was not a priest; and service vessels [the printed edition suggests: that were not consecrated as service vessels]; and the vessels of the asheira: they were of the asheira’s vessels.

messages.text: Continues on 29a: the eight go on: without service vessels, with vessels used for an asheira, with the wood of an asheira, an animal set aside and one worshipped.
